channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Economic Amnesty for Small and Medium Businesses Until 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan has announced an economic amnesty for small and medium-sized businesses, valid until December 31, 2026. The initiative, named "Second Chance," aims to write off penalties on tax debts if the principal amount is paid by the deadline. It also allows businesses to correct past tax reporting errors without penalty.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Calls for Strict Punishment of 'Enemies of the People'
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov demanded severe punishment for individuals allegedly receiving foreign funds to destabilize the country. Speaking at a security forces assembly, he stressed the importance of "iron discipline" and professionalism. A large-scale security operation involving 15,000 personnel is underway for upcoming international events.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan-China Forum: Chamber of Commerce chief proposes new cooperation model
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and China should shift from trade to joint production and industrial cooperation, proposed Temir Sariev, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry. He suggested establishing 100 operating joint ventures, not just memorandums, to attract investment, create jobs, and boost exports.

item.title: Nepal, China landslide floods kill 543; Kyrgyzstan reports no citizens affected
item.description: Floods triggered by a landslide in Tibet have killed 538 people in Nepal and five on the China-Nepal border, with hundreds still missing. A glacial lake overflow threatens further disaster. Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Ministry reported no Kyrgyz citizens were among the dead or missing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes Three-Year Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a three-year moratorium on inspections of small business entities. This measure, outlined in a presidential decree, aims to protect entrepreneurs. Exceptions apply to investigations related to criminal cases, human health, labor law compliance, citizen appeals, VAT refunds, and business liquidations.

item.title: India and Uzbekistan Expand Cooperation Across Multiple Sectors
item.description: India and Uzbekistan are deepening their strategic partnership, expanding cooperation beyond pharmaceuticals and trade into logistics, IT, energy, and defense. High-level visits and agreements, including around 20 documents signed during President Mirziyoyev's 2018 visit, have solidified bilateral ties. A virtual summit in 2020 further strengthened their robust partnership.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Several Personnel Changes August 24-28
item.description: Kyrgyzstan experienced several personnel changes between August 24-28. Nurbek Bukuev was appointed Deputy Minister of Health, replacing Bakytbek Kadyraliev. Aman Turgunaliyev became deputy director of the Department of Urban Development and Architecture. Urmat Abdukaimov was named head coach of the national football team, succeeding Robert Prosinečki.

item.title: Third Kazakh Tourist Missing After Nepal Flood Disaster
item.description: A third Kazakh tourist is believed to be missing following a severe flood on the Nepal-China border. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry confirmed diplomatic efforts are underway with both countries to locate the missing citizens. The disaster, caused by a Himalayan glacier collapse, has claimed over 620 lives and left thousands missing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Customs Service to Expand Staff by 189 Positions
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an increase of 189 staff positions for Kyrgyzstan's State Customs Service. The decision aims to enhance the efficiency of the customs authority. The Directorate for Control over the Implementation of Decisions of the President and the Cabinet of Ministers will oversee the order's execution.

item.title: Bishkek restricts construction during SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction has imposed restrictions on construction and heavy machinery use in Bishkek for three days starting August 30. These measures aim to ensure safety and public order during the upcoming SCO Summit and World Nomad Games, and maintain transport infrastructure.

item.title: Kyrgyz-Chinese investment forum proposes new cooperation model focusing on joint production
item.description: The head of the Kyrgyz Chamber of Commerce and Industry proposed shifting from trade to joint production and industrial cooperation with China. He suggested establishing 100 operational joint ventures, which would attract investment, create jobs, and boost exports of high-value products.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev calls for nuclear powers to negotiate on eliminating weapons threat
item.description: On the International Day for Nuclear Test Ban, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev urged nuclear powers to negotiate and sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty. He highlighted Kazakhstan's voluntary renunciation of its nuclear arsenal and its commitment to global peace and security. Tokayev also noted public support for developing nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

item.title: Earthquake in China Felt in Kyrgyzstan, Intensity 5.5 at Epicenter
item.description: An earthquake in China with an intensity of 5.5 at its epicenter was felt in Kyrgyzstan. The seismic activity's origin was located in China, 106 kilometers southeast of the village of Echkili-Tash. Villages in Kyrgyzstan reported an intensity of 2 points.

item.title: Uzbekistan Celebrates 35 Years of Independence with New Tashkent Inauguration
item.description: Uzbekistan marked its 35th anniversary of state independence with a ceremony in New Tashkent. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated the nation, highlighting the opening of new educational and cultural buildings. The event featured a Guinness World Record-holding fountain, symbolizing the nation's strength and development.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Addresses Ceremony Marking Uzbekistan's 35 Years of Independence
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev addressed a ceremony celebrating Uzbekistan's 35th anniversary of independence, held in New Tashkent. He congratulated citizens and highlighted the opening of new university buildings and a Guinness World Record fountain. The president expressed confidence that New Tashkent will be a center of development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ministry of Sports Holds Dialogue with 15,000 Coaches
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Sports hosted an unprecedented open dialogue with 15,000 coaches and specialists from across the country. Discussions covered the current state of sports, coach challenges, and proposals for future development. New initiatives include improving sports school management and streamlining athlete ranking processes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Cash Compensation for Electricity Instead of Subsidized Tariffs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor is proposing a monthly cash compensation for electricity for low-income families receiving state aid. The compensation would cover the difference between the standard tariff and the subsidized rate. This aims to ensure all eligible families receive benefits, regardless of housing or registration status. The initiative requires an estimated 448.6 million soms from the state budget in 2027.

item.title: New Methodology to Assess Regional Economic Growth Potential Until 2030
item.description: The Institute for Macroeconomic and Regional Studies (IMRI) is developing a unified methodological approach to assess and forecast regional economic growth until 2030. This approach will evaluate regional economies based on three scenarios: inertial (maintaining current trends), target (achieving set indicators through investment and reforms), and passive (assessing potential losses due to risks).

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Presidential Affairs Agency Proposes Single Internet Traffic Operator
item.description: The Presidential Affairs Agency of Kyrgyzstan has proposed making 'ElKat' the sole operator for international internet traffic delivery and transit. This move aims to prevent cyber threats and unjustified price hikes for communication services. A presidential decree in July 2025 had already granted 'ElKat' temporary monopoly powers until August 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan aim to boost bilateral trade to $3 billion
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan plan to increase mutual trade to $3 billion by expanding transport-logistics ties and industrial cooperation. Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Jeyenbek Kulubaev stated that relations have reached an unprecedented level, with active development of economic ties and joint projects. The Uzbek-Kyrgyz Development Fund has approved 37 projects totaling over $100 million.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Public Participation in Environmental Decision-Making
item.description: A training seminar on preparing alternative reports for human rights treaties and the Aarhus Convention principles was held in Tashkent for NGOs. Organized by Uzbekistan's Human Rights Center and the National Association of NGOs, it aimed to expand public involvement in environmental decisions.

item.title: Uzbekistan announces seven national programs for upcoming years
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement seven national programs covering education, healthcare, economy, ecology, rule of law, community development, and foreign policy in the coming years. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced these plans during the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. The programs aim to make knowledge and skills the "main capital" for future development and ensure all youth acquire a profession.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister to Visit Uzbekistan for State Visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan on August 29-30 at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Discussions will focus on strengthening strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, health, and other economic sectors. Bilateral agreements are expected to be signed.

item.title: EAEU goods traceability system to launch September 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Tax Service announces the launch of a goods traceability system within the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) on September 1. This system aims to control the circulation of specific goods, including refrigerators, washing machines, and televisions. The mandatory use of electronic waybills will be canceled for these items.

item.title: Bishkek imposes construction work restrictions due to SCO and World Nomad Games
item.description: Bishkek has temporarily restricted construction work and the use of heavy machinery for three days starting August 30. The measures are intended to ensure security and public order during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit and the World Nomad Games. Energy sector officials urge caution near power facilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank aims to increase local currency financing
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to gradually increase local currency financing and focus more on direct foreign investment rather than external debt, according to Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov. This shift aims to mitigate currency risks historically associated with foreign currency borrowing. The market for soum-denominated financing is developing, with companies now issuing Eurobonds in national currency.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Sets Goal to Reach $300 Billion Economy by 2030
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced a new goal to increase Uzbekistan's economy to $300 billion by 2030. He stated that the next decade will be a period of national growth, achievable through the nation's intellect, labor, and unity. The government plans seven national programs, focusing on education, healthcare, and high-tech economic models.

item.title: Nepal Floods Death Toll Rises to 538, with 977 Missing
item.description: The death toll from floods in Nepal has reached 538, with 977 people reported missing, according to the National Emergency Operation Center. Among the missing are 517 foreign nationals. The floods, triggered by a landslide on the Nepal-Tibet border, have destroyed homes, roads, and infrastructure. China reported five deaths and 558 missing in Tibet.

item.title: Azerbaijan presents tourism potential in Tashkent to boost bilateral cooperation
item.description: Azerbaijan's Tourism Bureau held a presentation in Tashkent showcasing the country's tourism potential to enhance cooperation with Uzbekistan. The event gathered tourism businesses from both nations, focusing on strengthening ties, sharing experiences, and promoting Azerbaijan as a year-round destination.

item.title: Trial for Kyrgyz citizen detained in Turkey set for September 9
item.description: The trial for Kyrgyz citizen Ermek Sabirzhanov, detained in Turkey on suspicion of links to the "Hizmet" movement, is scheduled for September 9 in Izmir. Sabirzhanov is currently held in Sincan prison in Ankara. He was arrested on May 22 at Ankara's Esenboğa Airport while traveling with his family. Turkish authorities accuse him of ties to FETO.

item.title: Uzbek President meets Singapore's Senior Minister, discusses investment and partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. They noted dynamic growth in trade and joint ventures, with Singaporean investments reaching $2 billion. Plans were agreed to expand investment and develop strategic partnership programs.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to attract foreign investment as a single region: Timur Ishmetov
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to diversify sources of foreign direct investment and avoid dependence on a single region or country, stated Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov in an interview with the Financial Times. While China is a major partner, Uzbekistan is strengthening ties with Europe and the US. The goal is to maintain good relations with many countries.

item.title: International Investment Forum Opens in Syrdarya Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: An international investment forum, "Do Business in Syrdarya!", has commenced in Syrdarya, Uzbekistan. The two-day event aims to showcase the region's investment potential to international businesses, foster new partnerships, and sign mutually beneficial agreements. Over 300 foreign investors from 20 countries are participating.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Committee Discusses Factors for Sustainable Economic Growth
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate Committee on Budget and Economic Issues discussed measures and results related to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) month. Committee Chairman Erkin Gadoyev highlighted that SDGs are linked to state budget parameters and social spending, with significant funds allocated to poverty reduction, education, and healthcare.

item.title: UNEP: Global Lake Pollution Could More Than Double by Mid-Century
item.description: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) warns that global lake pollution may more than double by mid-century. Lakes, crucial for freshwater supply and biodiversity, are under-resourced, especially in developing nations. Pollution from fertilizers, pesticides, and industrial waste degrades water quality and habitats.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Liberalize Water and Utility Tariffs, Central Bank Head Says
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to complete the liberalization of tariffs for water and other communal services currently regulated administratively. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov told Financial Times that this process, alongside currency and energy reforms, contributed to inflation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows State to Buy Shares of Systemically Important Banks Facing Collapse
item.description: Starting September 6, the government or a national holding company can acquire shares of systemically important banks at risk of collapse using state funds. The National Bank and the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market have approved the procedure for such intervention.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Fully Independent in Monetary Policy Decisions, Says Chairman
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is fully independent in making key interest rate decisions and conducting monetary policy, according to Chairman Timur Ishmetov in an interview with Financial Times. He stated the bank faces no government pressure in its decisions.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Lays Wreath at Monument of Independence
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited "New Uzbekistan" park and laid a wreath at the Monument of Independence. The monument reflects the nation's history, scholars, commanders, and significant events. The ceremony was held on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the country's independence.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tightens Energy Audit Requirements for Businesses
item.description: Starting September 6, Kazakh businesses must more accurately calculate energy consumption per unit of production. Audits will include measurements in winter and summer, and assessments of modernization benefits. "Eyeballing" savings is prohibited; calculations must be supported by measurements and technical data.
